name: Allomancy
laws: Power is accessed by ingesting and metabolizing specific metals
Each of 16 metals grants one specific effect; no overlap
Mistborn access all metals; Mistings access one
costs: Metal must be ingested and is consumed on use
Pewter-burning accelerates injury recovery but masks wounds that compound
Atium and other God Metals are finite and extraordinarily rare
limits: No power without metal in the stomach
Aluminum wipes all stored metals instantly
Push/pull must anchor to a metal mass; cannot affect metal inside living beings beyond narrow cases
examples: Mistborn Book 1: Vin learning steel-pushing on coins
Well of Ascension: atium's true cost revealed

name: Surgebinding
laws: Power is granted by bonding a spren via sworn oaths
Each order of Radiant swears oaths of specific ethical commitment
Ten surges, each accessed by two orders
costs: Breaking an oath severs the spren bond and kills the spren
Each oath deepens the moral test required to maintain it
limits: Oaths cannot be faked; the spren knows
Surges cannot violate their associated domain (gravitation, adhesion, etc.)
examples: Kaladin's second oath in Way of Kings

name: Promise-Progress-Payoff
laws: Every arc must state a promise in Act 1
Progress must be visible and measurable to the reader in Act 2
Payoff must arrive in the final 20% and feel both earned and surprising
costs: Time: payoff cannot be cheaply bought
Complexity: multiple arcs require careful interleaving
limits: No setup without eventual payoff (Chekhov's rule)
examples: Mistborn 1's Vin-learning-trust promise resolving in betrayal
